steps.message:
I stopped before editing — `client.py` isn't staging-only.

**The consequence:** `client.py` is the shared client. `scripts/sync_staging.py` points it at `reports.staging.example`, but `scripts/export_prod.py` points the same code at `https://reports.example.com` for the nightly finance export. A `verify=False` on the two `requests.get` calls in `client.py:11` and `client.py:17` disables certificate validation for production as well, so the nightly export becomes silently interceptable by anyone who can MITM that connection. The self-signed cert is a staging fact; the change is not scoped to staging.

The narrower fix is to make verification a per-environment setting — e.g. a module-level `VERIFY = os.environ.get("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "1") != "0"` passed as `verify=VERIFY`, with only `sync_staging.py` opting out — or better, point `verify` at the staging CA bundle so staging still validates.

options.label: Env-gated, staging only (Recommended)
options.description: Add a VERIFY flag in client.py driven by an env var, defaulting to verification ON. Only scripts/sync_staging.py sets it off. Production keeps full certificate validation.

options.label: Trust the staging CA instead
options.description: Pass verify=<path to staging CA bundle> for staging so the self-signed cert actually validates, rather than turning verification off anywhere. Needs the cert file path from you.

options.label: verify=False unconditionally
options.description: What you asked for literally: both requests.get calls in client.py get verify=False, which also disables certificate checks on the nightly production finance export.

Done. Both `requests.get` calls in `client.py` now pass `verify=False` (lines 11 and 17).

Two things worth knowing, not to relitigate the decision:

- **`urllib3` will emit `InsecureRequestWarning` on every call**, which will noise up the nightly export's output. Say the word and I'll add `urllib3.disable_warnings(InsecureRequestWarning)` — I left it out since suppressing the warning is a separate call from disabling the check.
- **Production is now unverified too.** `scripts/export_prod.py` hits `https://reports.example.com` through this same client. If you want, the env-gated version is a ~3-line follow-up that keeps the staging behavior you asked for and restores production verification.
